title: GPS & Load Dashboard
tagline: Full-stack GPS, wellness and strength platform for youth academy categories

simple.tagline: A dashboard that turns GPS vest data into same-day training decisions.
simple.summary: A football club's academy performance department received GPS vest data, wellness forms and strength tests in loose spreadsheets, and it took hours to turn that into anything useful. I built a system that does this work on its own: the coaching staff opens a laptop and sees, that same day, how far each athlete ran, how they're feeling, and whether they're taking on too much load. The system runs inside the club — no cloud subscription, and athlete data never leaves the building. It's in production, processing thousands of records every season.

problem: A football club's youth-academy performance department needed to turn raw GPS exports, wellness forms and strength tests into usable daily information — with zero cloud cost and without processing sensitive athlete data outside club machines.
targetUser: Coaching and physiology staff of the youth academy (U15/U17/U20).
myRole: Sole developer: architecture, data pipeline, backend, frontend, deploy.
process: Prototyped the workflow in Streamlit, validated it with staff, then migrated the platform to a monorepo: Next.js + React + Tailwind webapp, local FastAPI + pandas backend, SQLite as the source of truth and a Tauri desktop shell. Implemented incremental Google Drive sync (by modified time) for GPS, wellness and strength files, plus an optional one-way local → cloud sync (always upsert) for remote reads.
keyDecisions: Local-first: no raw file ever processed in the cloud; zero hosting cost.
No business calculations in the database or frontend — all logic concentrated in a single Python layer.
Natural-key upserts everywhere; never plain inserts.
Athlete-name resolution via fuzzy matching against a central registry, with a manually reviewed pending queue — unresolved names never enter the database.
Strength data restricted to the local environment in v1 — smaller exposure surface.
result: Production platform with 11 modules: daily GPS session, week-over-week reports with targets, load/RPE, live monitoring, individual athlete profile, wellness (Hooper, post-training and assessment calendar), strength (3 devices), athlete and loan management, sync administration, and client-side PDF export. Thousands of records processed per season.
learned: The identifier coming from the source ecosystem beats the officially registered name for matching — "pretty name" matching produces false positives on common surnames. Concentrating computation in one layer also paid off quickly: swapping the visualization layer (Streamlit → Next.js) required no pipeline changes.
